metadata.title: Name It, Own It, Date It.
metadata.description: A CLI-explainer for Sanjana on project management: turn a messy project status update into a clean RAID log — Risk, Assumption, Issue, Dependency — each one typed, owned, and dated, with the gaps (no owner / no date) flagged. Show the prompt, the real classification code, and the lines sorting themselves into four lanes. Framework-first, one revision, falsifiability, scaffolded task. Watermarked @HumanitariansAI.
metadata.note: CLI spine: B00 INTRO (Sanjana) · B01 PROBLEM+FRAMEWORK (RAID = R/A/I/D + owner/date rule, before examples) · B02 ASK(list the risks) · B03 CODE(v1 naive) · B04 OUTPUT(v1 flat pile) · B05 CHANGE · B06 CODE(v2 classify) · B07 OUTPUT(v2 four lanes + gaps) · B08 SUMMARY+falsifiability · B09 NEXT STEPS · B10 OUTRO(HaiOutro @HumanitariansAI). Output beats = RaidBoard motion. Composer beats carry folderLabel @HumanitariansAI.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN — composer, custom Sanjana greeting, @HumanitariansAI in the chrome
beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Liam for Sanjana, and this video is about using a Gen A I tool to turn a messy project status update into a clean RAID log — risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies, each one owned and dated.

props.command: claude "turn this project status update into a RAID log — risk, assumption, issue, dependency; each one owned and dated"

beats.role_note: the stakes, then the RAID framework shown as a STRUCTURE before any example

qc.sparse_reason: Framework card: four RAID type definitions + the owner/date rule on cream, shown before any example, like a title card; edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: Here's the problem. Every status update is a wall of worries, and the moment you ask A I to just list the risks, it calls everything a risk — including the things already on fire. So here's the frame that fixes it. RAID sorts every line into four types. A Risk might happen, and would hurt. An Assumption you're treating as true but haven't checked. An Issue is already happening, right now. A Dependency means you're blocked, waiting on someone else. And the rule that does the work: if an item has no owner or no date, it isn't tracked — it's just a worry.

props.title: THE RAID FRAME
props.caption: No owner or no date? It isn't tracked — it's just a worry.

beats.narration_text: Let's build it with Claude. Here's a real status update from a launch week. First pass — the move most people make: just ask it to list the risks.

props.command: claude "list the risks in this status update"

beats.narration_text: Read it before you trust it. All this does is walk the update line by line and stamp risk on every one. Clean list — and completely untyped. The server that's already down and the thing you're only assuming land in the very same pile.

props.title: raid.py

beats.role_note: MOVING output — RaidBoard flat pile, everything a 'risk', no owner/date
beats.narration_text: Run it. Seven lines, every one labeled risk. No types, no owners, no dates. The staging server is down right now — that's not a risk, it's an issue — but you'd never know it from this. One flat pile tells you nothing about what to do first.

props.title: WHAT "LIST THE RISKS" GIVES YOU
props.caption: One pile. Everything a risk — nothing typed, owned, or dated.

items.item: Staging server down since Monday
Could miss the App Store review window after the 25th
Payment vendor's API might change before launch
Waiting on Legal to sign off on privacy policy
New onboarding screens may confuse users
Analytics is under-counting installs right now
Marketing assets may not be ready

beats.narration_text: Here's the fix. Don't list risks — classify. For every line, pick the type: Risk, Assumption, Issue, or Dependency. Pull the owner and the date. And flag anything with no owner or no date as a gap.

props.command:
claude "don't list risks — classify each line as
  Risk / Assumption / Issue / Dependency; pull owner
  and date; flag any with no owner or no date"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the classification a flat list can't do
beats.narration_text: Now the model returns structured rows — item, type, owner, date — and your code does the part a flat list can't: it drops each line into its lane, and marks a gap wherever the owner or the date is missing.

props.title: raid.py

beats.role_note: MOVING output — RaidBoard four lanes, gaps flagged; the change made visible

qc.sparse_reason: Focused RAID board: four R/A/I/D lanes of owned, dated items with two gaps flagged; a board reads with whitespace by design, like the action-items table. Edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: Re-run. Same update — a completely different object. Every line is now typed, owned, and dated. Look what the sort caught: the staging server and the analytics bug moved out of risks and into Issues, because they're already happening. The legal sign-off is a Dependency, not a risk — you're blocked, waiting. And two assumptions nobody owns are flagged in orange, surfaced before they bite you.

props.title: THE RAID LOG · TYPED, OWNED, DATED
props.caption: Two assumptions nobody owns — flagged before they bite.

items.item: Could miss the App Store review window after the 25th
New onboarding screens may confuse first-time users
Assuming the payment vendor's API won't change before launch
Expecting marketing assets ready — QA hasn't seen them
Staging server down since Monday — blocks integration tests
Analytics is under-counting installs right now
Waiting on Legal to sign off on the privacy policy

qc.sparse_reason: Focused RAID board with a limits note; a board reads with whitespace by design. Edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: So the method is one move on any status update: type it, own it, date it. Two honest limits. The model can mis-type — it'll call an issue a risk if the wording is vague — so check the tense: is it happening now, or might it happen? And it can't invent an owner nobody named. No owner, no date? It isn't tracked yet.

props.title: THE METHOD
props.caption: Type it, own it, date it.
props.note: It can mis-type — check the tense, and verify the owner.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud; addressed to Sanjana
beats.narration_text: Your turn, Sanjana. Take your next status update, paste this prompt, and let Claude classify every line as a Risk, Assumption, Issue, or Dependency — with an owner and a date — then list anything missing an owner or a date as a gap you have to close. Run it each week, and your RAID log keeps itself.

props.command:
claude "here's my status update. Classify every line
  as {item, type: R/A/I/D, owner, date}, group by type,
  and list every item with no owner or no date as a GAP
  I need to close."
